newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu's adviser visited Gulf -Israeli report.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu's adviser visited Gulf -Israeli report.

text.p: Israel's Maariv newspaper said on Friday an aide to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu visited the Gulf to try to warm up cool relations with Arab states ahead of an international economic forum in Switzerland.
Netanyahu's office declined comment on the report that foreign policy adviser Dore Gold had visited Qatar and possibly Oman during a secret mission lasting 24 hours.

The two states have raced ahead of the four other Gulf Arab states in establishing economic ties with Israel but stopped short of diplomatic relations pending a resolution of all Arab-Israeli conflicts.

Protracted Israeli-Palestinian negotiations over the West Bank town of Hebron that ended in an accord in January put a strain on budding relations. Qatar welcomed the accord, calling it an important step for Middle East peace.
Maariv said Gold's assignment was to "warm up relations between Israel and the Gulf states" and to set up meetings between Netanyahu and Gulf foreign ministers at the World Economic Forum in Davos.
The newspaper did not spell out what was accomplished during the adviser's trip. Netanyahu left for Davos on Friday.
